Ralston names the region Little-Russia, not a people; recording it as Ukrainians is the draft's mapping (by analogy with Bohemia to Czechs), a translation choice the page neither confirms nor contradicts. The grade's second people rests on this row.

grade_rationale.text: Machal records the silvan spirit Lésiy, Lésovik for the Russians, and names no source for it on these pages.
Ralston records the Lyeshy among Russian peasants of the Olonetsk and Archangel Governments and of Perm, Vyatka and Vologda, citing no other author in these passages.
Ralston records the Lyeshy as the protector of the wolves in Little-Russia, recorded here as Ukrainians; this second people rests on that single Ralston passage.
Afanasyev records the лѣшій and its regional names from Russian provinces and districts, and the belief that they vanish underground for the winter.
Ralston's tale of the Leshy in Russian Folk-Tales cites Afanasief, so it is counted with Afanasyev and not as a separate source.
Machal, Ralston and Afanasyev are three independent authors, and the verified peoples are Russians and Ukrainians, so the grade is widely-attested.
